title: round-trip.yaml description claims resumed_at coverage but no flow step asserts it
evidence:
+  styled radios), smart-resume landing on the first INCOMPLETE step, and
+  resumed_at stamping on the first post-resume save.
detail: The description advertises resumed_at stamping as covered, but Flow steps 1-7 assert only the draft row/continue_token, sent status, banner, value restore, stepper landing, and confirmation. No step verifies resumed_at, so the claimed coverage is never exercised.
recommended_fix: Add an explicit resumed_at assertion to the flow (e.g. extend the post-submit DB check), or remove the resumed_at claim from the description.

title: {SCENARIO} truncation wording ambiguous — truncating the whole local part can eat {RUN_ID}
evidence: +   - `{SCENARIO}` → the scenario slug **sanitised for email local-parts**: `/` replaced with `-` (e.g. `happy-path/employed-with-rental-history` → `happy-path-employed-with-rental-history`), and the whole local part truncated to 64 chars.
detail: The recommended pattern is `test+{SCENARIO}-{RUN_ID}@example.com`. If 'the whole local part' is truncated at 64, long slugs (e.g. `edge-cases-coapplicant-same-email-as-primary`) push {RUN_ID} past the cut, destroying cross-run uniqueness and breaking duplicate-detection and token-seam lookups.
recommended_fix: State that truncation applies to the sanitised slug contribution only, preserving the full `{RUN_ID}` suffix, or define an explicit truncation order.

title: monthly_income_cents "4100" implies £41/month for an employed accountant
evidence:
+  employment_status: "employed"
+  job_title: "Accountant"
+  employer_name: "Ledger & Co"
+  employment_duration: "4 years"
+  monthly_income_cents: "4100"
detail: If the field is truly cents, 4100 = £41.00/month — implausible for the persona and a candidate tripwire for any server-side income plausibility or affordability check. If the field is pounds, the _cents suffix is misleading.
recommended_fix: Confirm the unit; if cents, use a realistic value (e.g. 410000); if pounds, rename the scenario field to match.
